active-directory-and-windows.description: Active Directory and Windows endpoint attacks
active-directory-and-windows.notes: sized-with-reason per D-02: 7 members (below 8 target); scope-expanded from the `ad` D-01 starter (4 AD-only skills, below <5 merge threshold) to include Windows lateral movement, privilege escalation, and AV evasion; the broader Windows-platform cluster shares the same OS substrate. Further merge into linux-and-post-exploit rejected because mixing Windows and Linux/macOS tooling violates D-04 skill-content topicality.

binary-exploitation.notes: renamed from the `binary` D-01 starter to make scope explicit; includes both exploitation primitives (heap, ROP, format string) and reverse-engineering/analysis tooling because the two halves share the same skill substrate.

crypto-attacks.notes: sized-with-reason per D-02: 7 members (below 8 target); renamed from the `crypto` D-01 starter and scope-expanded to include blockchain/web3 attacks (smart-contract-vulnerabilities, defi-attack-patterns — 2 skills, below <5 merge threshold). Combined under the shared 'crypto' terminology as the security community uses it; if downstream curation wants a separate blockchain bucket later, the move is trivial.

linux-and-post-exploit.notes: absorbs the original `payloads` D-01 starter via D-02 merge (only 2 candidate skills, below <5 merge threshold). reverse-shell-techniques folded here under the post-exploit umbrella; unauthorized-access-common-services folded into recon. No standalone `payloads` bucket survives.

mobile.notes: sized-with-reason per D-02: 3 members (below 8 target and below the <5 merge threshold); kept standalone because natural merge candidates (active-directory-and-windows for OS-platform parity, linux-and-post-exploit for post-exploit umbrella) would mix mobile and desktop/server platforms, violating D-04 skill-content topicality.

recon.notes: sized-with-reason per D-02: 6 members (below 8 target); kept standalone because merging into another bucket would mix recon with attack execution and violate D-04 skill-content topicality.

server-side-execution.description: Server-side code execution and trust-boundary chains
server-side-execution.notes: split from the `injection` D-01 starter along the server-side-execution subtopic axis per D-02 >15 policy.

web-client-attacks.notes: split from the `injection` D-01 starter along the client-driven and browser-policy subtopic axis per D-02 >15 policy.

web-injection.notes: originally part of the `injection` D-01 starter (~35 skills); split along the natural subtopic axis into web-injection / web-protocol-attacks / web-client-attacks / server-side-execution per D-02 >15 policy.

web-protocol-attacks.description: HTTP protocol-layer attacks and request flow abuse
web-protocol-attacks.notes: sized-with-reason per D-02: 7 members (below 8 target); standalone because merging into web-injection (10) would land at 17 and force another split along the same protocol-vs-payload axis.

ai-and-supply-chain.description: AI/ML security and software supply chain attacks
ai-and-supply-chain.notes: catch-all per D-06 (themed): 3 members (below 8+ D-03 emergent threshold); coherent thin theme — AI/ML + supply-chain skills share a 'trust boundaries in modern software pipelines' frame. Per-member reason tag per D-05: standalone.

forensics-and-misc-recovery.description: Forensics, memory analysis, and steganographic recovery
forensics-and-misc-recovery.notes: catch-all per D-06 (themed): 3 members; coherent thin theme — forensics-flavored skills (memory analysis, network forensics, steganographic recovery) share a 'recover hidden state from collected artifacts' frame distinct from the offensive-playbook shape of primary topical buckets. Per-member reason tag per D-05: standalone.

hack-skills-routers.description: Category routing and skill-selection entry points
hack-skills-routers.notes: catch-all per D-06 (themed): 7 members; D-05(b) misfit — these are meta-navigation router skills (the upstream's *-sec / *-vuln / top-level hack router skills), not topical playbooks. Per-member reason tag per D-05: redundant. Phase 3 may revisit whether to expose this bucket as a marketplace plugin or exclude it entirely.
